tip: Schwer means hard or difficult here, not physically heavy: Aller Anfang ist schwer = every beginning is difficult.
With separable verbs, zu slips between prefix and stem: wieder plus sehen becomes wiederzusehen, written as one word.
After a definite article a neuter adjective ends in -e: das kaputte Fahrrad, never das kaputt Fahrrad.
After ein with a neuter noun the adjective takes -es: ein schönes Bild. The -es marks the neuter that ein hides.
Zu always takes the dative, and zu plus der contracts to zur: zur Schule = to school.
Many strong verbs shift a to ä in the du and er forms: fahren becomes er fährt.
Danken uses für for what you thank someone for: danken für Ihre Hilfe, not danken über.
Time you spend takes the accusative with no preposition: den ganzen Nachmittag = for the whole afternoon.
Genitive shows possession: die Geschichte dieses Landes = the history of this country. Masculine and neuter add -es.
Empfehlen shifts e to ie in the du and er forms: sie empfiehlt, like sehen and lesen.
Begegnen takes the dative, and dative plural nouns add -n: wir begegnen alten Freunden.
Trotz means despite and takes the genitive: trotz ihrer Erkältung = despite her cold.
Sein builds its own perfect with sein, not haben: wir sind gewesen = we have been.
Any infinitive can become a capitalized neuter noun: kochen to das Kochen. Vor dem Kochen = before cooking.
Herein adds motion toward the speaker: hereinkommen = to come in, toward me. Her always points to the speaker.
The idiom einen Blick werfen auf means to take a look at. Here werfen means cast, not literally throw.
Viertel vor sechs = quarter to six, literally a quarter before six. Vor counts down toward the hour.
Werden means to get or become for changing states: es wird dunkel = it gets dark.
Verbs like vergessen add a zu-infinitive set off by a comma: Ich habe vergessen, die Milch zu kaufen.
Sich etwas anschauen uses a dative reflexive: ich schaue mir einen Film an = I watch a film for myself.
For exercise Germans say Sport treiben, not Sport machen: er nimmt sich vor, Sport zu treiben.
Hin marks motion away from the speaker: zur Schule hin = off to school. Her would point back toward you.
Fertig means done or ready, and etwas fertig machen means to finish it: ich mache das Abendessen fertig.
Use nach for cities and countries meaning to: nach Hamburg = to Hamburg, with no article.
Eigen means one's own and still needs a possessive and adjective ending: sein eigenes Geschäft = his own business.
